Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java` with 25 self-contained JUnit 5 test methods covering `DateUtils`: the `add*` methods, `truncate`/`ceiling`/`round` (Calendar/Date/Object overloads, including `ArithmeticException` for huge years, `ClassCastException` for invalid types, `IllegalArgumentException` for unsupported fields, SEMI_MONTH boundaries), the `getFragmentIn*` family, `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`, the day-range `iterator` (including exhaustion/`remove()`/invalid style), `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly`, the `set*` field setters with their valid ranges and `IllegalArgumentException` boundaries, `toCalendar`/`toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, and `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`. Behavior for tricky cases (rounding thresholds, fragment arithmetic) was empirically verified against the real implementation before encoding as assertions.

`./_tools/test.sh` compiles and runs it cleanly: **25/25 tests pass**, no other files were modified.
